core_problem_solved: To provide an open-source Java library for parsing and extracting information from HTML documents, designed to be tolerant of malformed, real-world HTML that does not strictly adhere to standards.
key_features: Parsing HTML into a traversable node tree
A visitor pattern for processing nodes in the tree
A filtering system with predicates for finding specific tags or content
era_and_niche: One of the early, popular HTML parsers for Java, widely used for web scraping and content analysis in the early-to-mid 2000s.
reason_for_obsolescence: The library is **completely obsolete**. It has been unmaintained for over a decade (since around 2006). The modern, actively maintained, and feature-rich de facto standard for all HTML parsing and manipulation in Java is **`org.jsoup:jsoup`**.
